subject: Urgent: emergency inference stability patch — immediate customer advisory
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@acme-data.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Oct 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Urgent: emergency inference stability patch — immediate customer advisory

Hi Olivia —

We’ve detected a small set of user requests (including some from Acme) that experienced degraded or truncated model outputs over the last hour. Our runtime team traced this to a rare KV-cache race that can surface when variable-length batching and prefix sharing occur across certain model variants.

To prevent further customer impact we will be pushing an emergency hotfix to the inference runtime in the next ~40 minutes. The change closes the race and adds an additional integrity check on shared KV segments; the fix has a small CPU/GPU performance delta but prevents the corruption mode.

What to expect:
- Window: deploying now; expected completion within 45 minutes for affected regions (no full-service restart).
- Impact: short (5–15s) connection resets for warm requests as nodes swap the patched runtime; we do not expect data loss.
- Rollback: we have a tested rollback that can be applied within 20 minutes if any regression is observed.

We’re attaching the hotfix patch summary and the rollback checklist (see attachments). Important notes for Acme:
- No request payloads leave your tenancy; this is a runtime memory integrity issue, not a data exfiltration vector.
- We will run a targeted recheck on all recent requests from your account after deployment and surface any anomalies.

Action requested from you: please either confirm you’re OK with this immediate patch or let us know if you require us to wait (we can coordinate a scheduled window but it will increase exposure). If you have a procurement or legal hold, say so now and we’ll pause.

I’ll send an update when the patch is live and again after post-deploy verification. Apologies for the short notice — we’re treating this as P1.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Technical Account Manager | Redwood Inference
attachments: 2028-10-kvcache-hotfix.patch (summary), rollback-procedure.txt (checklist), customer-qa-notes.pdf

Tessa —

Thanks for the heads up. Two quick Qs: 1) Will this require us to rotate any keys or update client-side SDKs? 2) Can you confirm whether any in-flight requests might have been returned with partial results (we noticed a few short responses in our logs at ~08:45UTC)?

We’re generally OK with you proceeding, but if the patch affects our response consistency we may need a roll-forward plan for the rest of the day.

—Olivia
Olivia Grant

Hi all —

Quick technical clarifications in response to Olivia:
1) No client-side changes required. The patch is entirely server-side; no API version bump, no key rotation.
2) We are running request-level integrity scans now. Preliminary logs confirm a small number (~0.02% of requests in the affected pool) saw truncation or early EOS tokens. We will run a full scrub of Acme’s recent 24h requests and share timestamps/ids for anything we find.

Deployment status: staging verification passed on three model families. We will deploy to canary hosts first, then roll across the cluster with health gating. If we see higher-than-expected error rates post-deploy, we will pause and initiate the rollback procedure in rollback-procedure.txt (attached).

Security note: this is a memory consistency bug. No evidence of data exfiltration, no network-layer compromise. We’ve alerted security and have audit logs retained per your tenancy policy. Rafael — I need the quick compliance blurb for Acme to reassure them on logs/audits.

Vivek
Principal Engineer, Runtime

Date: Sat, 06 Oct 2028 10:05:02 +0000
Subject: Re: Urgent: emergency inference stability patch — immediate customer advisory

Hi Olivia —

I’m Rafael from Product Security & Compliance. Short answer to your concern about exposure: our post-incident audit will include immutable request logs (request IDs, timestamps, model variants) and system memory snapshots around the affected windows. We will provide: 
- A CSV of Acme’s request IDs with timestamps for any requests showing truncation or non-conformant outputs.
- Proof of retention: audit-entry IDs and S3 URIs (read-only) where logs are stored per our tenancy SLA.
- Statement that no process showed outbound network connections initiated from the runtime during the fault window.

We’ll redact any customer payloads where required by contract, but we will provide sufficient detail for your security team to validate there was no data leakage. Expect the initial audit bundle within 3 hours and the full report within 48 hours.

I’ll also note that our deployment is in progress: canary hosts healthy. Will update when we hit 25%/50%/100% rollout.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Product Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

We’ll review the audit bundle when it arrives. If the initial scrub shows >0.1% impact to Acme requests we may request a coordinated rollback window later today.
